title: hotkey-fairness-and-admission-gradient-for-console-metrics-ingress
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Console metrics ingest is vulnerable to tenant 'hotkeys' (high-volume tenants or routes) that cause local queue saturation, elevated P95/P99 latencies, and backpressure cascades. Existing admission control is binary and causes either unfair drops for small tenants or high latency for critical customers.

Goal: Introduce a priority-gradient admission controller and local spillover strategy that enforces per-tenant fairness while keeping overall token-level throughput high and bounded latency within SLOs. The controller should be pluggable in the current ingress stack and operate without global coordination in the common case.

Scope: API gateway / ingress proxies -> local in-memory priority buckets -> adaptive admission gradient -> controlled spillover to persistent queue -> circuit-breaker thresholds. Work includes design, implementation, integration tests, dashboards and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress can gracefully throttle top 5% of tenants by volume while maintaining 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for median tenants under synthetic microburst tests
No tenant should see silent drop rates > 1% during steady-state; hot tenants allowed to be degraded with explicit drop metrics
Local spillover to persistent queue must maintain strict ordering for tenant-scoped streams and have bounded retry windows (configurable up to 30s)
Controller is feature-flagged and can be toggled per-region; rollout runbook documented and tested
Observability added: per-tenant admitted rate, drop rate, queue-depth, backpressure-events, and fairness-index metric
comments: 2026-02-12: Asha Patel - Initial writeup and hypothesis posted. Suggested local-only controller to avoid cross-region coord complexity.

2026-02-20: Marco Rivera - Prototype of per-worker priority buckets implemented. Observed tail latency improvement in synthetic tests but throughput decreased ~6% under skewed load. Investigating lock contention in bucket map.

2026-02-26: Design review - Preferred 'gradient' admission (soft percentage reduce) over hard token caps to allow graceful degradation. Product recommends exposing per-tenant priority tiers for paid customers.
2026-03-02: UX/PM feedback - Add explicit telemetry for when a tenant is in 'degraded' mode so downstream customers can alert. Also request per-route labels for billing mapping.
2026-03-05: Marco Rivera - Implemented spillover writer to persistent queue; added idempotent keys and tenant-ordered checkpoints. Integration tests for ordering pass locally.

2026-03-09: Ops - Canary in us-west-2 started at 10% ingress. Early metrics: top-1% tenants drop rate increased to 4.1% (expected), median tenant P95 reduced from 210ms->95ms. Need to tune gradient slope to reduce drop for mid-tier tenants.
2026-03-10: Asha Patel - Updated acceptance criteria and added runbook steps for rollback, throttle adjustments, and smoke checks to the canary doc. Marked for follow-up tuning sprint.
implementation_notes: Architecture: AdmissionGradient component sits after decoding layer and before batching adapter. It computes a soft admission probability p(t) for each tenant based on recent admitted rate, queue depth, and configured priority weight.
State: Keep a small ring buffer of recent admission outcomes per tenant (sampled) to compute exponential moving averages. Persist minimal checkpoint (tenant -> last-offset) for spillover handoff.
Performance: Use lock-free sharded maps (64 shards) for bucket state to avoid contention. Avoid heap allocations in hot path; use preallocated buffers for sampled metrics.

Trade-offs: Local-only controller avoids cross-region coordination cost and provides fast decision-making; downside is temporary per-worker unfairness when tenant traffic routes unevenly. To mitigate, include probabilistic smoothing across deployments during scaling events.
Fallbacks: If AdmissionGradient throws or is misconfigured, default to existing admission logic (conservative cap) to avoid data loss. Feature flag with circuit-breaker is mandatory.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in CI with simulated tenant skews
2) Internal canary in staging with reproduction of hotkey bursts
3) Canary in us-west-2 at 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor fairness-index and P95
4) Gradual ramp to 25% with operator tuning, then to 100% if stable
5) Post-rollout: 72-hour observation window and automated regression checks on release branch
